extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys and agents), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline, and practitioners subject to USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and sanctions applied by the USPTO Director/OED in disciplinary proceedings against registered patent practitioners, focusing on trust accounting, record-keeping, remedial education, suspension, and administrative consequences. The page is a Final Order approving a settlement for violations of the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners registered to practice before the Office in patent matters are subject to the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, 37 C.F.R. § 11.101 through 11.901.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At all times relevant, Respondent was registered and therefore subject to the Rules. This is the baseline authority for evaluating practitioner conduct before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO jurisdiction for disciplinary proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has jurisdiction over disciplinary matters pursuant to 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32, and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.26.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory and regulatory provisions authorize the Office to investigate and impose discipline on registered practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safekeeping property / trust account requirement (37 C.F.R. § 11.115)
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must keep client funds separate from their own funds and must keep client trust account records as required by 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violation example: between ~Nov 2014 and Jan 2016 Respondent failed to deposit approx. $12,480 in advance fees and USPTO fees into a client trust account, deposited those funds into the law firm operating account, and drew funds for personal and business expenses from the account holding client funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record-keeping exception and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may qualify for an exception to 37 C.F.R. § 11.115 if records are kept in compliance with a state in which the practitioner is licensed (exception in § 11.115(l)(4)), but failure to keep such records means the exception does not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent did not keep records in compliance with any of the States in which he is licensed and therefore did not meet the exception of 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(l)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating and mitigating factors considered in discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office considers recognition of seriousness, remedial actions taken, prior disciplinary history, and other factors when determining sanctions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation noted: Respondent recognized the seriousness, resubmitted payments to the USPTO, opened a client trust account, and had no prior USPTO discipline. The record may be used later as an aggravating factor in future proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice as sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner may be suspended from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark and other non-patent matters as discipline for violations of the Rules of Professional Conduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter the agreed sanction was a 90-day suspension commencing on the date the Final Order is signed, and suspension continues until the OED Director grants reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is ordered to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order affirmatively requires compliance with § 11.58 as part of the sanctions (the Order states 'Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58').

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement procedures and compliance (37 C.F.R. § 11.60)
rubrics_metrics.description: A suspended practitioner remains suspended until the OED Director grants a petition for reinstatement pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, and must comply with § 11.60 when requesting reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states Respondent shall comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.60 upon any request for reinstatement to practice before the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education (CLE) remedial requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners may be required to complete CLE as part of discipline; here Respondent must complete at least ten (10) credit hours covering trust accounting and law office practice management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The CLE requirement is imposed to remediate deficiencies in trust accounting and practice management identified in the misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative dissociation from USPTO systems (Customer Numbers and PKI)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate a disciplined practitioner's name from all USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificates and the practitioner shall not apply for or obtain a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order directs prompt dissociation and bars applying for a Customer Number unless and until reinstated to practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public disclosure of disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order in the OED's FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the Order's notice text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice summarizes the suspension, the rule violated (37 C.F.R. § 11.115), and states the action resulted from a settlement agreement under the cited statutory/regulatory provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of a disciplinary proceeding when addressing subsequent complaints, in future disciplinary proceedings as an aggravating factor or to rebut statements, and when considering requests for reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order explicitly reserves the Office's right to use the record for these purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of costs in disciplinary settlements
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties to the settlement each bear their own costs incurred to date and in carrying out the Agreement and Final Order unless otherwise stated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order provides that the OED Director and Respondent shall each bear their own costs.
